reason: The description is remarkably thorough and accurate. It correctly captures all major behavioral branches: metadata derivation, runner instantiation via transformer, partitioning, serial/in-band logic, event-emitter vs callback branching with the exact five events, the watcher-interrupted guard, empty-test-suite and leak-detection failure paths, bail-early logic, snapshot cleanup and failure flagging, run-level error handling with rethrow vs suppression, and final success computation. One minor gap: the description says the inner catch (runner execution errors) 'records the run-level execution error' and 'reports run completion', but in the implementation that behavior only happens in the *outer* catch — the inner catch simply suppresses the error when the watcher is interrupted and rethrows otherwise; it does not itself call `onRunComplete` or set `runExecError`. Also, the description omits that `onRunStart` passes `showStatus: !runInBand` as part of the start notification options, and that event subscriptions are explicitly unsubscribed after `runTests` completes. These are minor omissions that don't materially affect implementability.
missing_functionality: Event listener unsubscription after runTests completes (the unsubscribes loop)
onRunStart is called with showStatus: !runInBand in the options object
The inner try/catch only suppresses errors when watcher is interrupted and rethrows otherwise — it does not set runExecError or call onRunComplete (that is the outer catch's job)
incorrect_or_misleading_points: Bullet 9 conflates the inner and outer catch blocks: it says 'records the run-level execution error, reports run completion, and rethrows' as if this applies to runner setup/execution errors generically, but only the outer catch does all three; the inner catch (runner execution) only conditionally rethrows or suppresses
